title: RWB-006: Claude Code skill for Review While Building
description:
Create a portable Claude Code skill (or custom slash command) that injects the Review While Building protocol into any Claude Code session, regardless of repository.

The skill should:
- Be installable globally (not per-repo AGENTS.md)
- Instruct Claude Code to:
  1. Break implementation work into discrete, reviewable steps
  2. Create a Sherpa session via HTTP API with the plan
  3. After implementing each step: compute diff, push to Sherpa, check feedback
  4. Structure steps for reviewability (foundational first, group by concept)
  5. Check for developer feedback between steps and adjust if needed
- Include the Sherpa API base URL (configurable, default localhost:5150)
- Handle error cases (Sherpa not running, API failures)
- Provide clear output to the developer ("Step 3 pushed to Sherpa for review")

The skill should be compatible with Claude Code's skill loading mechanism.
Research how OpenCode handles equivalent functionality (custom commands/plugins).

Acceptance criteria:
- Developer can invoke skill from any repository
- Agent correctly creates Sherpa session and pushes steps
- Agent checks feedback between steps
- Works without any per-repo configuration
- Clear developer-facing output

title: Sherpa — AI-Guided Code Review Tool
description:
Sherpa is a single-user local tool that pairs a developer reviewing code changes (branch diffs) with an AI guide. The developer points Sherpa at a local Git repository, and the tool analyzes the current branch's changes against its merge base. An AI (via opencode or claude CLI) provides a project summary, change analysis, and step-by-step guided review. The developer walks through each step, chatting with the AI, and validates changes as they go. Review progress is persisted to disk.

Stack: Loco.rs (Rust backend), HTMX + FlyonUI (UI), diff2html (client-side diff rendering), devbox for dev environment.

As a developer, I want the project bootstrapped with Loco.rs, devbox configuration, and basic dependencies so that I have a working foundation to build on.

- [ ] devbox.json configures packages, env vars, and init hooks

- [ ] A README.md documents how to devbox shell && cargo run to start the app
- [ ] The app starts and responds on localhost with a basic health check endpoint

title: US-010: Review completion summary screen
description:

- [ ] Unfolding a card shows: step title, files involved, the AI explanation, and the chat messages from that step

title: US-011: Review state persistence and resume
description:

- [ ] Resuming restores the user to the last un-validated step with all previous state intact

title: RWB-003: Agent HTTP API — Complete step endpoint

Endpoint details:
- Auth: Bearer {agent_token} header

- Developer can immediately see and review the step in Sherpa UI
- AI explanation generates automatically if not provided

title: RWB-009: NeedsRevision step state and blocking feedback
description:
Add NeedsRevision state to the step state machine and optional blocking feedback.

Changes:
- New StepStatus: NeedsRevision (developer flags a step for agent revision)
- UI: "Request Revision" button on step page (alongside Validate)
- When developer requests revision: step status → NeedsRevision
- check_feedback endpoint returns needs_revision: true for that step
- Optional block_agent flag on session (developer can toggle "Pause agent")
- Agent's check_feedback sees blocked=true and should pause
- Agent instruction set (skill) teaches agent to handle NeedsRevision

Step state machine becomes:
  Planned → ReadyForReview → Reviewed
                            → NeedsRevision → ReadyForReview (agent re-pushes)

Acceptance criteria:
- Developer can request revision on a step
- Agent sees NeedsRevision in feedback response
- Block/pause mechanism works
- Agent skill handles the pause/revision flow

- Plan steps are visible in guide page (all showing Planned status)

- Invalid requests return proper error JSON

title: RWB-004: Agent HTTP API — Check feedback endpoint
description:
Implement GET /api/agent/sessions/{id}/feedback — agent polls for developer feedback between steps.

Endpoint details:
- Auth: Bearer {agent_token} header
- Response: { steps: [{ step_number, status, comments: [{ role, content, timestamp }] }] }
- Returns all steps with their current status and any chat messages
- Only returns steps that have comments or status changes since last check (use query param ?since=timestamp)
- Reuses existing chat_messages table/model

Acceptance criteria:
- Agent can poll for feedback via curl
- Developer comments left via step chat appear in feedback response
- Step validation status reflected in response
- ?since parameter filters to recent changes only
- Auth required

title: Review While Building — Live Progressive Code Review
description:
Enable developers to review AI agent's completed implementation steps in real-time while the agent continues building subsequent steps. This eliminates the "wait for agent to finish, then review everything" workflow.

Core concept: An AI coding agent (Claude Code, OpenCode, etc.) implements a feature in discrete steps. After completing each step, it pushes review data (diff, explanation, file list) to Sherpa via HTTP API. The developer reviews completed steps in Sherpa's existing review UI while the agent continues.

Key architectural decisions:
- HTTP API first (universal, any agent can curl), MCP server wraps it later
- Agent pushes diffs (agent knows exactly what changed, avoids race conditions)
- Agent decides step granularity (conceptual grouping for reviewability)
- Feedback loop: developer comments flow back to agent via check_feedback endpoint
- Extends existing ReviewSession/ReviewStep models (~80% code reuse)
- Agent instruction delivered via portable skill/command (not per-repo AGENTS.md)

Phases:
1. MVP: Agent HTTP API + Live session mode + UI step status badges
2. Agent skill/command for Claude Code and OpenCode
3. Feedback loop (developer comments → agent)
4. MCP server (wraps HTTP API)
5. Advanced: NeedsRevision state, blocking feedback, step reordering
close_reason: duplicate — existing epic guided-review-z6m already has all tasks

title: RWB-010: Step plan reordering and amendment
description:
Allow the agent to reorder or amend unstarted plan steps mid-implementation.

New endpoint: PATCH /api/agent/sessions/{id}/plan
- Can replace/reorder steps that are still in Planned status
- Cannot modify ReadyForReview or Reviewed steps
- Can append new steps to the end
- Can remove Planned steps
- Updates step numbering accordingly

Complexity: Step reordering affects ai_analyses cache keys (step_number), chat_messages (step_number), and validated_steps. Need careful handling.

Acceptance criteria:
- Agent can reorder Planned steps
- Cannot modify completed steps
- UI reflects updated plan
- Existing analyses/chat preserved for completed steps
